newsitem.title: USA: Clinton, Greenspan hold regular meeting on economy.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Greenspan hold regular meeting on economy.

text.p: President Bill Clinton and his economic team had a regular meeting with Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan on Wednesday to discuss the state of the U.S. economy, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.

"As he does periodically, the president and his economic team met with the chairman of the Federal Reserve to discuss the state of the economy and issues related to the economy," McCurry told reporters.

McCurry said the meeting's participants included Vice President Al Gore, outgoing White House chief of staff Leon Panetta, his incoming replacement Erskine Bowles, Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin, Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers, Office of Management and Budget Director Franklin Raines and National Economic Council chairman Gene Sperling.
Asked how often Clinton and Greenspan meet, McCurry replied: "They get together I think every several months to share views about their outlooks on the economy."
"For reasons that everyone here understands, that's about all that I am going to say about the meeting," McCurry said, adding only that the meeting had lasted about an hour.
